subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of these elements is an alkali metal found in Group 1?
questions.explain: Lithium is in Group 1, the alkali metals, while chlorine is Group 7, argon Group 0 and magnesium Group 2.

questions.q: How many electrons are in the outer shell of a Group 1 element?
questions.explain: All Group 1 elements have a single electron in their outer shell, which they lose to form 1+ ions.

questions.q: What happens to the reactivity of the alkali metals as you go down Group 1?
questions.explain: Reactivity increases down Group 1 because the outer electron is lost more easily.

questions.q: Why does the reactivity of the alkali metals increase down the group?
options: The outer electron is further from the nucleus and lost more easily
The atoms gain electrons more readily
The nuclear charge decreases down the group
The atoms become smaller down the group
questions.explain: Larger atoms have their outer electron further from the nucleus with more shielding, so it is lost more easily.

questions.q: When an alkali metal reacts with water, which two products are formed?
questions.explain: Alkali metals react with water to give a metal hydroxide plus hydrogen gas, e.g. sodium gives sodium hydroxide and hydrogen.

questions.q: A small piece of sodium is dropped onto water. Which set of observations would you expect?
options: It floats, moves on the surface and fizzes
It sinks and glows red hot
questions.explain: Sodium is less dense than water so it floats, and the hydrogen produced makes it fizz and move around the surface.

questions.q: What is the pH of the solution formed when an alkali metal reacts with water?
questions.explain: The metal hydroxide formed is soluble and alkaline, giving a pH greater than 7.

questions.q: Which of these elements is a halogen in Group 7?
questions.explain: Chlorine is a Group 7 halogen, while sodium is Group 1, neon Group 0 and calcium Group 2.

questions.q: How many electrons are in the outer shell of a Group 7 element?
questions.explain: Halogens have seven outer-shell electrons, so they gain one electron to form 1- ions.

questions.q: What is the colour and state of chlorine at room temperature?
questions.explain: Chlorine is a yellow-green gas at room temperature.

questions.q: What is the state of bromine at room temperature?
questions.explain: Bromine is a red-brown liquid at room temperature, between gaseous chlorine and solid iodine.

questions.q: What happens to the reactivity of the halogens as you go down Group 7?
questions.explain: Reactivity decreases down Group 7 because gaining an outer electron becomes harder.

questions.q: Why does the reactivity of the halogens decrease down the group?
options: The outer shell is further from the nucleus so an electron is gained less easily
The atoms lose electrons more easily
The nuclear charge increases so electrons are gained more easily
The atoms become smaller down the group
questions.explain: As atoms get larger down the group, the outer shell is further from the nucleus with more shielding, so an extra electron is attracted less strongly.

questions.q: Chlorine is added to a solution of potassium bromide. What are the products of this displacement reaction?
questions.explain: Chlorine is more reactive than bromine, so it displaces bromine to form potassium chloride and bromine.

questions.q: Bromine is added to a solution of sodium chloride. What would you expect to observe?
options: No reaction, because bromine is less reactive than chlorine
Chlorine gas is displaced and bubbles off
The solution turns dark grey as iodine forms
questions.explain: A less reactive halogen cannot displace a more reactive one, so bromine does not displace chlorine from sodium chloride.

questions.q: Given lithium, sodium, potassium and rubidium, which would react most vigorously with water?
questions.explain: Reactivity increases down Group 1, so rubidium, the lowest of these, reacts most vigorously.

questions.q: What is the common name given to the elements in Group 0?
questions.explain: Group 0 elements, such as helium, neon and argon, are called the noble gases.

questions.q: Helium has only 2 outer electrons yet is placed in Group 0. Why?
options: Its outer shell is full, as the first shell holds only 2 electrons
It reacts like the other noble gases despite having a partial shell
It was placed there by mistake in the periodic table
questions.explain: The first shell can hold a maximum of two electrons, so helium has a full outer shell and behaves as an unreactive noble gas.

questions.q: Why are the noble gases very unreactive (inert)?
options: They have a full outer shell of electrons
They readily lose their outer electrons
They have only one outer electron
questions.explain: A full outer shell is stable, so noble gases have little tendency to gain, lose or share electrons.

questions.q: What happens to the boiling point of the noble gases as you go down Group 0?
options: It falls to below zero for all of them
questions.explain: Boiling points increase down Group 0 as the atoms get larger and intermolecular forces get stronger.
